Mig.KeepBothHint: The copy gets new IDs, its own boot files (bcdboot) and its own C: mapping, so you can choose either disk in the firmware boot menu.
Mig.Next.KeepBoth:
1. Restart and open the firmware boot menu (often F8, F11, F12 or Esc).
2. Choose "Windows Boot Manager" of the new disk. Its entry may be listed with the disk's model name.
3. Windows on the new disk starts with its own C:. The old installation remains as it was and can still be chosen.
4. To make the new disk the default, change the boot order in the firmware settings.
Mig.Next.Replace:
1. Shut down the computer (do not restart).
2. Either remove the old disk, or open the firmware boot menu (often F8, F11, F12 or Esc) and choose the new disk.
3. Windows starts as before. Check the disk in Lasteast, then extend C: into any unallocated space on the new disk.
4. Keep the old disk unchanged for a few days before reusing it.
Mig.PrepNote: After step 1 has been applied, come back here: the plan is recalculated from the new layout.
Mig.ReplaceHint: The copy is identical, including disk and partition IDs, so Windows starts from it unchanged. Until you remove the old disk or boot from the new one, Windows keeps the copy offline.
Mig.Subtitle: Copy Windows and its boot partitions to another disk, typically a new SSD. Your current Windows keeps running and is only read; partitions in use are copied from a shadow copy.
Mig.Trouble:
• Reconnect or select the old disk: it was never changed, so you can always go back.
• UEFI vs BIOS: a GPT disk needs UEFI mode, an MBR disk needs Legacy/CSM. Check the firmware setting.
• BitLocker may ask for the recovery key after the hardware change; have it ready (account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey for Microsoft accounts).
• "INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE": the new disk's controller may need a different storage driver (e.g. RAID/Intel RST vs AHCI). Boot the old disk, install the driver, migrate again.
• Boot files: the Lasteast rescue environment (Boot Recovery) can rebuild them with bcdboot.

Planned.Desc.BootRecovery: Boot repair, EFI and boot-entry management, and Lasteast Rescue Boot media (USB/ISO) based on properly licensed Windows PE.
Planned.Desc.Cleanup: Find temporary and unnecessary files; you choose what is removed, with Recycle Bin support.
Planned.Desc.DiskClone: Clone disks and partitions (intelligent or sector-by-sector) with compatibility checks and verification.
Planned.Desc.DiskConversion: MBR ↔ GPT, FAT32 ↔ NTFS and basic ↔ dynamic conversions, each clearly marked with its data-loss risk.
Planned.Desc.DiskHealth: SMART and NVMe health, temperature and wear monitoring with configurable alerts.
Planned.Desc.FileOperations: Browse partitions, copy and move files, and find files that prevent a partition from shrinking.
Planned.Desc.FileRecovery: Recover deleted files from NTFS and FAT32 volumes, including volumes of lost partitions, to another disk.
Planned.Desc.OsMigration: Move Windows to a new SSD or HDD, preserving boot configuration, with post-migration verification.
Planned.Desc.PartitionManagement: Create, delete, format, resize, move, merge and split partitions through a validated operation queue.
Planned.Desc.PartitionRecovery: Quick and deep scans for lost or deleted partitions, with previews. Recovered data is never written to the source disk.
Planned.Desc.PerformanceLab: Sequential and random benchmarks, surface scan and latency monitoring. Write tests are explained before they run.
Planned.Desc.SmartFix: Scan the computer, explain storage problems by severity, and offer previewed, confirmed fixes.
Planned.Desc.StorageAnalyzer: Treemap of disk usage by folder and file type, with large, old and duplicate file finders.
Planned.Desc.Technician: Disk inventory reports (PDF/CSV/HTML), batch workflows, portable mode and a command-line interface.
Planned.Desc.Tools: Partition table viewer, hex viewer, alignment checker, file system checker and secure wipe.
Planned.Desc.VirtualDisks: Create, attach, expand and compact VHD/VHDX files, clearly separated from the host disk.
Planned.Note: This module is not available in this build. Nothing on this page reads from or writes to your disks.
